item.title: Aspects of $\mathcal{N}=2$ SUSY gauge theories and applications to Quantum Field Theory and Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.15619v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This thesis investigates the application of techniques developed in supersymmetric gauge theories to physical problems in Quantum Field Theory and Gravity, focusing on the Seiberg-Witten (SW) curve and its quantum version. After reviewing the essential concepts of Supersymmetry and the derivation of the SW curve, we explore its applications in both fields. In Quantum Field Theory, we investigate the emergence of Argyres-Douglas theories in the moduli space of supersymmetric models, focusing on extremal correlators. We analyze a conformal model to compute their instanton corrections, finding agreement with predictions from Effective Field Theory, and discuss the implications for analogous observables in Argyres-Douglas theories. In Gravity, we exploit the quantum SW curve and its relation to differential equations describing physical systems. We establish the linear stability of Topological Stars, arising in the fuzzball proposal, under massive charged scalar perturbations. We also investigate charge superradiance in configurations with a horizon and derive a novel hypergeometric representation of the confluent Heun function, relevant to gravitational-wave propagation in the Schwarzschild background. This result yields a new resummed expression for waveform tail contributions, in excellent agreement with numerical data. Finally, beyond the SW formalism, we develop a Machine Learning algorithm based on Hamiltonian Neural Networks to reproduce the geodesics of a neutral particle in a fuzzball geometry. For critical trajectories, our method outperforms standard numerical integrators in both efficiency and accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Cipriani

item.title: New topological phase transitions in $\kappa$-deformed $\phi^4$ lattice models
item.description: arXiv:2610.15644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper explores topological phase transitions in the momentum space of the $\kappa$-deformed $\phi^4$ lattice model within the mean-field approximation. We show that the double-well structure of the momentum space gives rise to degenerate momentum states at high energies and that this change is marked by a phase transition. We investigate this transition using both numerical and analytical methods, with the analytical approach based primarily on singularity theory. Our numerical analysis shows that the energy at which the topological phase transition occurs is related to the noncommutative parameter by the simple power law $E \sim 1/\alpha^{4}$. By mapping the constant-energy-level surface to the $A_{3}$ singularity, we obtain the same result analytically. We also present results unique to noncommutative systems, showing that the fraction of particles in degenerate momentum states has a nonzero commutative limit. As a nonperturbative effect, this result provides a testable prediction for the existence of noncommutative spacetime.
item.dc:creator: Adith A, A. Bhagwat

item.title: Higher Dressing and Shift-Invariance in 4D Topological BF Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.15737v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A characteristic feature of topological field theories is the absence of local propagating degrees of freedom. In four-dimensional BF theory with cosmological term, we make this feature manifest by exactly reducing the finite non-Abelian shift symmetry. We do so by identifying a higher dressing field, a 1-form compensating the shift, allowing to build from first principles the composite shift-invariant field $\boldsymbol{B}=B-\lambda^{-1}F$. In terms of this dressed field, the dynamics becomes algebraic and sets $\boldsymbol{B}=0$, directly exposing the absence of local propagating degrees of freedom. This provides the first explicit instance of the higher-form Dressing Field Method.
item.dc:creator: J. Fran\c{c}ois, L. Ravera

item.title: Nonperturbative optomechanics with thin, weakly reflective intracavity dielectrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.15749v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Levitated dielectric sensors are often treated as perturbative probes of a pre-existing optical field. We show that this picture fails for a novel sensor geometry: a dielectric plate whose transverse extent captures the full optical mode. Even an optically thin sensor with modest refractive index can heavily restructure the intracavity fields, effectively partitioning a cavity into two subcavities with substantial cross-coupling and producing new optical resonances and trapping sites with properties which deviate from the standard intuition. Conventional perturbative expressions for the cavity frequency shift and optomechanical coupling depart from the exact solution at thicknesses as small as $\sim\lambda/(10n)$. Furthermore, cavity locking decreases the coupling and increases the trap stiffness by orders of magnitude, and the coupled subcavity structure permits appreciable optical cooling at zero detuning, a distinct behavior unique to this nonperturbative regime. These effects, sharing a common origin, establish a distinct regime of cavity optomechanics in which the sensor is no longer merely a probe of the cavity field, but an element that helps define it.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Laeuger, Nancy Aggarwal

item.title: Random wave chaos on momentum-fractionated microstate geometries
item.description: arXiv:2610.15918v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the role of momentum fractionation in the development of chaos on smooth 3-charge supergravity solutions of D1-D5 theory, specifically momentum-fractionated superstrata. We probe the chaos through the dynamics of null geodesics and waves. On fractionated backgrounds, both geodesics and waves show uniformly strong chaos (large chaotic sea and near-perfect agreement with the Berry random wave hypothesis). In contrast, geodesics and waves on single-mode (non-fractionated) superstrata are closer to separability (although still chaotic). We discuss a possibility that such dichotomy can be related to the expectation that monotone BPS states are less chaotic than fortuitous ones. Finally, we explain why our chaos probes are meaningful for microstate geometries even though they become trivial in the black hole limit.
item.dc:creator: Vladan Djuki\'c, Mihailo \v{C}ubrovi\'c

item.title: Equation of State Classification of Core-Collapse Supernovae with a Network of Gravitational-Wave Detectors
item.description: arXiv:2610.16130v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Gravitational waves from core-collapse supernovae may provide a unique probe of the equation of state (EOS) of dense nuclear matter. In previous work, we assessed the potential of machine-learning methods for EOS classification for rapidly rotating supernovae using individual gravitational-wave detectors. Here, we extend the framework to detector networks and investigate the impact of detector configuration, source distance, arrival time, and sky location on the classification. Using convolutional neural networks, we perform 10-class EOS classification directly from noisy detector data for both second- and third-generation observatories. We find that detector geometry strongly influences classification performance. For Galactic events, current detector networks can achieve promising classification performance, but the reach depends sensitively on the detector network antenna response. Adding detectors improves time-averaged performance and produces more uniform classification across the sky. Third-generation observatories extend the classification reach to 100 kpc for favorable source orientations but do not remove the dependence on detector geometry.
item.dc:creator: A. Akhmetali, Y. S. Abylkairov, J. A. Font, M. Zanolin, E. Abdikamalov

item.title: Retarded Green Function For Bopp--Podolsky Electrodynamics in Four-Dimensional De Sitter Spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2610.16239v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study classical Bopp--Podolsky (BP) electrodynamics on four-dimensional de Sitter spacetime, focusing on its transverse retarded Green function and gauge-invariant electromagnetic response. Because de Sitter spacetime is maximally symmetric, its vector Green functions admit a covariant expansion in a finite basis of invariant bitensors, with scalar coefficients depending only on the invariant separation. For conserved sources, the fourth-order field operator factorizes into Maxwell and massive-vector operators, yielding the BP retarded kernel as the difference of their transverse Green functions. Using the invariant bitensor decomposition, we reduce the propagator equations to a hypergeometric master equation and determine the distributional structure of its solution. The common leading short-distance singularity of the Maxwell and massive-vector sectors cancels, leaving a logarithmic master singularity and a softened vector-potential wavefront. After one curl, the gauge-invariant field-strength kernel contains a null-cone delta distribution and a regular timelike tail. The smooth Maxwell master tail is annihilated by the curl, so the interior electromagnetic tail is generated entirely by the massive sector. We also derive an exact horizon-regular static potential, demonstrate the cancellation of the Coulomb divergence, recover the flat-space BP potential, and formulate the generalized Gauss law. On global de Sitter spacetime, the compactness of the spatial sections requires the total charge to vanish; we implement this constraint using an antipodal charge configuration with smooth factorized initial data. The analysis is classical and does not assume a quantum Lee--Wick contour or a preferred de Sitter vacuum.
item.dc:creator: Wei Fan, Xiao Yan Chew

item.title: Sensitivity of calibration-free DESI DR2 BAO--supernova constraints to a distance-duality tilt
item.description: arXiv:2610.16496v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent measurements from DESI baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) have reported a moderate preference for dynamical dark energy, challenging the standard $\Lambda$CDM paradigm. Nonetheless, such a trend could reflect a tension between the shape and the offset of the Hubble diagrams predicted by current BAO and Type Ia supernovae (SN) data, which may underpin a possible breakdown of the cosmic distance duality relation (CDDR) linking luminosity distances $D_{\rm L}$ and angular-diameter distances $D_{\rm A}$. We explore this possibility by parametrizing deviations from this relation as $\eta(z) \equiv D_{\rm L} / [{(1+z)}^2 D_{\rm A}] = \alpha{(1+z)}^\varepsilon$, and investigate how the preference for a Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) dynamical dark energy is modified once $\varepsilon \!\neq\! 0$ is allowed. Using DESI DR2 and uncalibrated SN data (Pantheon$+$, DES-Dovekie, Union3, and Union3.1), we find that allowing $\varepsilon$ to vary freely in both $\Lambda$CDM and CPL reduces the CPL preference with respect to $\Lambda$CDM by a larger amount than the addition of spatial curvature $\Omega_k$; only Union3.1 exhibits comparable reductions. We also find that the preference reduction is robust to alternative $\eta(z)$ parametrizations, and that the $\eta(z)$ constraints remain stable under the removal of BAO tracers or low-redshift cutoffs for Pantheon$+$, whereas the DES-Dovekie preference largely disappears once $z < 0.1$ SN are removed. In a separate calibrated analysis, illustrative Planck sound-horizon and SH0ES absolute-magnitude priors give $\alpha \simeq 0.942 \pm 0.014$, quantifying the normalization mismatch under those assumptions. We also map the CDDR violation onto photon-loss and varying-$G$ scenarios, concluding that the cosmological constraints are much weaker than existing constraints on these physical mechanisms.
item.dc:creator: St\'ephane Fay, Mikel Artola, Leandros Perivolaropoulos

item.title: CosmoAgent: AI Agent for Theoretical Cosmology
item.description: arXiv:2610.16536v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present CosmoAgent, an agentic AI framework using large language models (LLMs) to search for dark-energy and modified-gravity models. We define a covariant grammar that allows LLM agents to explore the space of modified-gravity Lagrangians. An in-house computational pipeline derives the equations of motion, solves the background dynamics, and evaluates the likelihood using late-time expansion data, including the DES 5-year type Ia supernova sample and the DESI Data Release 2 BAO measurements. Theories are ranked by the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) to balance simplicity and likelihood. We benchmarked 8 frontier LLMs from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Kimi, DeepSeek, and Qwen, and all LLMs are able to find theories with a lower nominal AIC than flat $\Lambda$CDM, with a best improvement of $\Delta$AIC = -3.328. Seven recover quadratic quintessence. Exploratory searches also return induced-gravity and scalar-Gauss-Bonnet structures. The modest AIC improvements do not establish an observational preference for these models over flat $\Lambda$CDM. The code is publicly available at wsunamoutlook-prog/AI-Modified-Gravity.
item.dc:creator: Stephon Alexander, Loukas Gouskos, Savvas M. Koushiappas, Cooper Niu, Wenrong Sun

item.title: TheoPhysEval: Assessing AI agents at autonomous theoretical physics problem solving
item.description: arXiv:2610.16733v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. Without AI assistance, a typical problem in our collection could be solved by a world expert in about a day or less but would take considerably longer for experts in adjacent specialties. We test the ability of off-the-shelf AI agents to tackle these problems autonomously, without human hints. When given access to tools available in a realistic setting, including the ability to search the literature and write scripts for numerical and symbolic work, the best-performing agent, GPT-6-Astra harnessed in Codex, obtains the final answers with a near-perfect accuracy of 98% at an average cost under USD 3 per problem. On average, agents show only small changes in accuracy when denied web search and access to background research papers, suggesting significant memorization of the literature. These results suggest that state-of-the-art agents can accurately perform concrete calculations required across theoretical physics research. We comment on the broader implications of these findings and discuss possible explanations for the current lack of agent-led breakthroughs in theoretical physics despite their outstanding problem-solving abilities.
item.dc:creator: A. Ramesh Chandra, Aaghaz Mahajan, Ainesh Sanyal, Mianqi Wang, Shubhadeep Chakraborty, Sudip Chakraborty, Shailesh Chandrasekharan, Rama Govindarajan, Akshit Goyal, Jonathan J. Heckman, Yasir Iqbal, Divya Jaganathan, Saumav Kapoor, Andreas Karch, Pushkar Khandare, Sandeep Krishna, Anupam Kundu, Alok Laddha, Tongyan Lin, Swarnendu Maity, Nilmani Mathur, Shani Nadir Meynet, Alessandro Mininno, Abhijeet Mishra, Vidur Niranjan, Abhishodh Prakash, Pratik Rath, Durbar Roy, Debargha Sarkar, Srikanth Sastry, Gary Shiu, Aninda Sinha, Thomas Van Riet, Praneeth Netrapalli, Suvrat Raju

item.title: Evidence for Hierarchical Turbulent Scaling in Nearby Star-Forming Galaxies
item.description: arXiv:2610.16805v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We find recurring signatures of intermittency in molecular-gas velocities from cloud to galactic scales. In 31 selected galaxies from PHANGS-ALMA, velocity-centroid exponents through sixth order show nonlinear order dependence and nearly linear relations between consecutive exponents across galaxies. Positive estimated offsets from single-exponent scaling occur in all 52 galaxies with a valid power law fit and 99 of 100 clouds. A generalized She-Leveque hierarchy accommodates these signatures, supporting a hierarchical description of turbulent scaling in molecular gas across these environments.
item.dc:creator: Luna Maria Scipio, Fernando A. N. Santos, Jay Armas

item.title: Metric and dilaton information from high-overtone quasinormal modes of analytic Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton black holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.16973v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Black-hole interiors are hidden from exterior observers, yet their geometry can enter the high-overtone spectrum of linear perturbations. We study how this spectrum encodes metric and supporting-matter information in analytic Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton black holes. Coupling a neutral spectator to the dilaton at fixed UV dimension provides a matter-sensitive channel alongside the momentum response. For real-endpoint spacelike connections, the momentum response and mass-label dependence separate the metric exponents from the signed dilaton slope. Near the causal threshold, a complex endpoint controls the spectral family: the mass profiles approach a common value, producing a shared fractional correction, while regular propagation retains label dependence. This mechanism is present at criticality without an inner horizon and continues locally into timelike interiors. Exterior numerical spectra support the reconstruction and the leading complex-endpoint responses. Local scaling and probe coupling set the candidate responses, while wave connection determines their imprint on the exterior spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Yu Shi, Chikun Ding, Yuebing Zhou, Changqing Liu, Weike Deng, Sheng Long

item.title: Revisiting Critical Higgs Inflation: Electroweak Couplings, CMB Observables, and Perturbative Unitarity
item.description: arXiv:2610.17211v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We revisit the scenario of critical Higgs inflation, in which inflation is driven by the Standard Model Higgs boson with parameters chosen close to a critical point, giving rise to an inflection point in its potential. After reviewing this model, we perform a systematic study of its viability centered around three criteria: (1) consistency with electroweak-scale measurements, (2) ability to reproduce the cosmic microwave background (CMB) observables, and (3) sensitivity of the model predictions to unknown UV physics, based on a breakdown of perturbative unitarity. We first show that compliance with electroweak-scale measurements is controlled by the parameters in the Higgs potential at inflationary scales, also updating the literature values. We then demonstrate how for any choice of potential parameters, agreement with the CMB observables can be achieved through the choice of the nonminimal coupling, in both metric and Palatini formulations of gravity. However, we also find that there exist no regions of parameter space, in either the metric or Palatini formulations, in which compliance with all three physical criteria is possible. While this does not exclude the possibility of the Higgs field driving inflation, it means that predictions for any observable are in principle sensitive to the details of the model's UV completion.
item.dc:creator: Sarah R. Geller, Sol Gutierrez-Lara, David I. Kaiser, Thomas Steingasser

item.title: MRI Turbulence versus $\alpha$-Viscosity in Circumbinary Disks: Implications for Gravitational-Wave Dephasing and Accretion Variability
item.description: arXiv:2610.17212v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Our understanding of gas torques on massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) relies on hydrodynamical (HD) simulations of circumbinary disks (CBDs) in which an $\alpha$-viscosity models angular momentum transport. However, CBDs around MBHBs near merger are hot, magnetized plasmas where transport is driven by magnetohydrodynamical (MHD) turbulence sustained by the magnetorotational instability (MRI). We test how well an $\alpha$-viscosity captures MRI turbulence with 3D global Athena++ simulations of a locally isothermal CBD around an equal-mass, circular MBHB, run in HD and MHD from the same initial torus on identical grids, so that only the transport mechanism differs. Excising the region within twice the binary separation, $r<2~a_{\rm bin}$, allows $1000$ orbits of evolution, several times longer than previous MHD simulations. Both disks deliver the same accretion rate, and the gas beyond $2~a_{\rm bin}$ exerts a positive torque in both, yet the MHD torque is $3.5$ times larger and $3$ times more variable. Near the midplane, transport is similar in the disk body but three times weaker in MHD at the cavity edge, where $2$-$3$ times more mass piles up in a more eccentric cavity, raising the torque. The accretion rate is modulated mainly at twice the binary frequency in HD, but by a persistent lump at the cavity edge and its beat with the binary in MHD. The outer-disk torque therefore implies a contribution to the gas-induced phase shift in the gravitational-wave signal of LISA binaries $3.5$ times larger than in $\alpha$-disk models, and a different variability signature for LSST and Roman.
item.dc:creator: Mudit Garg, Yan-Fei Jiang

item.title: Quantum Reference Frames in terms of Tetrads
item.description: arXiv:2610.17225v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We adapt to the context of quantum theory the treatment, familiar in relativity theory, of a reference frame as a tetrad. Since a tetrad is a set of four orthonormal vectors at a spacetime point, it encodes a timelike direction, three orthogonal spatial directions, and units; and so it gives a configuration in spacetime (a spatial orientation and state of motion) of an idealized infinitesimal apparatus (``rulers and a clock"). So a natural ``first guess" is that the state of a quantum reference frame should be an assignment of complex amplitudes to a set of tetrads. We develop this idea, in terms of bundles over spacetime of bases of the tangent spaces. This paper is a companion to two other papers. It emphasises the main conceptual aspects of our proposal, while the other two papers give physical details. It also explains the main contrast between those two papers. Namely: (i) the first considers a single spacetime geometry, so that a quantum reference frame, on our proposal, gives a superposition of perspectives on that geometry; while (ii) the second considers the spacetime manifold with no geometry given a priori, which will imply that a quantum reference frame, on our proposal, can describe a superposition of perspectives on a superposition of geometries---not ``just" a superposition of perspectives on a single geometry. The main mathematical idea for representing this contrast will be choosing between (i) the orthonormal frame bundle, for a given spacetime geometry; (ii) the frame bundle in the usual sense of containing all bases of all spacetime points' tangent spaces.
item.dc:creator: Jeremy Butterfield, Daniel A. Turolla Vanzella

item.title: Love at First Loop: Quantum Deformability of Near-Extremal Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.17259v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The static Love numbers of black holes vanish in classical, four-dimensional, asymptotically flat General Relativity. We study how this changes for the response of near-extremal Reissner--Nordstr\"om black holes to a minimally coupled massless scalar, at energies where the Schwarzian mode of the near-horizon throat fluctuates strongly. The black hole then responds as a quantum system with a spectrum of states. Its static response is a polarizability, given by virtual transitions between them. For $\ell=0$ the static Love number vanishes, by the shift symmetry of the scalar, but for multipoles $\ell\geq1$ the static Love numbers are nonzero: the finite rotational energy of the spin-$\ell$ intermediate states spoils the cancellation responsible for the classical result. Since the throat no longer has a classical geometry from which to read off a tidal response, we define it through the retarded Green's function, and compute its full frequency dependence at leading order in $r_+\omega$. Its conservative part requires renormalization: the near-horizon theory fixes the coefficient of its logarithm, and with it a dependence on the energy that no local term can remove, while its finite local terms are matching data of the four-dimensional theory. The dissipative part is finite and scheme independent. For $\ell\geq1$, it vanishes at low frequencies when the energy is below the rotational gap, while at the gap threshold it becomes non-analytic in frequency and produces a late-time $t^{-3/2}$ tail.
item.dc:creator: Pablo A. Cano, Marina David, Roberto Emparan, Stefano Trezzi

item.title: Evading the Swampland de Sitter Obstruction via Thermodynamic Duality-Induced Horizon Corrections in Unimodular Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.17438v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the early-universe cosmological implications of Unimodular Gravity coupled to Power-Law Nonlinear Electrodynamics in the presence of quantum-corrected horizon thermodynamics derived from the principle of thermodynamic duality. By incorporating both logarithmic and inverse-area corrections to the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, we derive modified Friedmann equations exhibiting novel $H^4$ and $H^6$ terms that represent genuine quantum gravity effects. We demonstrate that these higher-order corrections become dynamically significant in the high-energy regime of cosmic inflation, naturally modifying the slow-roll dynamics without requiring a fundamental inflaton potential. A comprehensive phase-space analysis reveals that the quantum corrections drive early-time de Sitter-like attractors, providing a robust mechanism for sustained inflationary expansion. Confronting the model with the Swampland program, we show that the correction factor $\mathcal{F}(H)$ modifies the effective slow-roll parameters, enabling the model to satisfy the Swampland de Sitter and Distance conjectures during the inflationary epoch. We calculate the inflationary observables, including the spectral index $n_s$ and the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$, and demonstrate that the model's predictions are in excellent agreement with the Planck 2018 observational constraints. Our results suggest that thermodynamic duality-induced horizon corrections offer a viable and testable pathway for realizing successful inflation within a well-motivated quantum-gravitational framework.
item.dc:creator: Reza Baghbani

item.title: Resonant JPZ algebras and 3D Chern--Simons gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.17480v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work we construct three-dimensional Chern--Simons gravity theories for the six resonant $JPZ$ algebras generated by the Lorentz generators $J_a$, translations $P_a$, and an additional Lorentz-like generator $Z_a$. The resonance condition together with the Jacobi identities leaves precisely six configurations arising from the semigroup expansions. Our main result is that three of them, $B_4$, $\widetilde C_4$, and $C_4$, are isomorphic to $iso(2,1)\oplus so(2,1)$, although they yield different gravitational realizations when we keep the original $JPZ$ field identification fixed. For each case $JPZ$, we determine the invariant tensors, gauge curvatures, Chern--Simons action, field equations, and the corresponding maximal-rank coupling sectors. The field equations can be written in the compact form $\Omega_\sigma\mathbf F=0$, which makes explicit how the additional field $h^a$ contributes to the curvature, torsion, and the remaining gauge-curvature components. We use the direct-sum isomorphisms to classify the local metric sectors and to relate them to known global and asymptotic solutions, while keeping the gravitational interpretation tied to the original $(\omega,e,h)$ fields.
item.dc:creator: Remigiusz Durka, Nelson Merino, D. M. Pe\~nafiel

item.title: The Promise of Gravitational-Wave Astronomy
item.description: arXiv:2610.17647v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We review the promise of upcoming gravitational-wave (GW) observations in addressing some of the important open questions in astrophysics and cosmology. A decade after the first direct detection of GWs, the field is entering a transformative phase driven by progressive detector upgrades and the anticipated advent of space-based and next-generation ground-based observatories. These instruments will not only push the distance horizon of GW observations to cosmological redshifts, but will dramatically extend the accessible frequency band, opening entirely new source classes that lie beyond the reach of current detectors. The source landscape is rich enough that surprises are likely. This review surveys our current understanding across this landscape and offers some perspective on the discoveries that upcoming GW observations are poised to deliver.
item.dc:creator: Parameswaran Ajith

item.title: Spectrally enhanced gravitational redshift signals in photonic interferometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.18131v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum mechanics and general relativity are remarkably successful, yet their joint predictions remain beyond direct experimental reach. Photonic interferometers operating in a gravitational field offer a promising route to test this regime: gravitational redshift differentiates photon propagation between vertically separated arms, leading to a predicted phase shift and reduction in interference visibility. These effects are minute on laboratory scales, motivating existing proposals to consider large interferometer areas to accumulate them geometrically. Indeed, such schemes typically require kilometre-scale optical paths to produce appreciable interferometric signals. Here, we propose a strategy that replaces geometric accumulation with spectral enhancement by coupling the two interferometer arms to optical scatterers based on ultranarrow atomic transitions. These transitions serve as local spectral references: gravitational redshift changes the photon's detuning from each resonance, producing large differences in reflection amplitude and hence substantial visibility loss and interferometric phase shift already for centimetre-scale height differences. We quantify the experimental requirements and assess the feasibility of implementation with current or near-term technology. Our proposal thus opens a route to tabletop optical tests of the interplay between quantum mechanics and general relativity.
item.dc:creator: Jerzy Paczos, Piotr T. Grochowski, Natalia Bruno, Emanuele Distante, Stephan Welte, Magdalena Zych

item.title: Hypergeometric solutions to coupled Klein-Gordon equations in cosmology with small-field excursions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18586v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Klein-Gordon equation is a second order differential equation that appears in a variety of applications in mathematics, physics and engineering. This equation is often solved using numerical methods, since a general analytical solution is unattainable. However, one can find very useful analytical solutions for some special cases. In cosmology, the Klein-Gordon equation of a field can explain the physics of inflation and has important consequences on understanding the origin and evolution of the universe. An analytical solution to the Klein-Gordon equation in cosmology has been obtained in the small-field excursion approximation, and it turns out that the solution can be written in terms of the confluent hypergeometric limit function. In this work, we derive this result again while showing the details of the calculations and then generalize to the case of two coupled Klein-Gordon equations. We show that the solution of this coupled system can be written in terms of Kummer's hypergeometric limit function while considering minimal assumptions. We carry out a full numerical calculation of the coupled system and compare it to the results from the analytical expressions.
item.dc:creator: Amin Aboubrahim, Anastasiia Minenkova, Tomas Yonkers

item.title: Enabling Polyspectra via Stochastic Realizations of Inverse Decay Curvature Perturbations in Axion Inflation
item.description: arXiv:2610.18748v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Current and upcoming galaxy-redshift surveys offer a promising path for constraining inflationary physics. These constraints are often imposed by relating correlations of the primordial curvature perturbation to the late-time galaxy correlation functions. The primordial correlators can either be computed analytically, or via realizations of the primordial curvature perturbations that are initialized on a grid and evolved numerically according to the classical equations of motion. In this work we take a hybrid approach, initializing the fields in the Bunch-Davies vacuum; and then imposing time evolution through direct numerical integration. Our method efficiently generates realizations of the inverse decay primordial curvature perturbations for axion inflation---an inflationary model in which a pseudoscalar inflaton field couples to a $U(1)$ gauge field via a Chern-Simons interaction. Depending on the choice of parameter $\xi\in\{2, 2.5, 3\}$, which controls gauge field particle production in this model, our method generates realizations with an average runtime of a few hours on 1 CPU core. We compute the power spectrum and bispectrum from these realizations and find a surprisingly large discrepancy between our result and previous work that used an approximation for the gauge field mode functions---up to a factor of $\sim4$ difference for the bispectrum in the case of $\xi=2$. This new method enables not only rapid computation of higher order polyspectra, but also generation of initial conditions for large-scale structure analyses.
item.dc:creator: Matthew A. Reinhard, Zachary Slepian, Atsushi Taruya

item.title: Quantum Imaging as alternative readout in atom interferometry: The case of Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2409.03477v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a quantum imaging-inspired setup for measuring gravitational fields using an atom that emits a photon at one of two possible locations. The atom acquires a gravitationally induced quantum phase that it shares with the photon. By restoring the path identity of the atom after its interaction with the gravitational field, the gravitationally induced phase can be measured using photon interferometry without the need for additional measurements on the atom. Through repeated measurements with varying interferometric setups, the gravitational potential and inertial acceleration can be deduced.
item.dc:creator: Marian Cepok, Dennis R\"atzel, Claus L\"ammerzahl

item.title: Hybrid compact stars with finite strange quark mass and dark energy: implications for astrophysical observations
item.description: arXiv:2410.19029v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we present a detailed investigation of compact stars composed of deconfined quark matter, with finite strange quark mass ($m_s\neq0$), admixed with dark energy. The quark sector is described using the MIT bag model equation of state, while the dark energy component is assumed to satisfy a linear equation of state of the form $p^{de}=\omega\rho^{de}$, where $\omega$ lies in the range $-1\leq\omega\leq-\frac{1}{3}$. The stellar configuration is studied within the Finch-Skea ansatz for the $g_{rr}$ metric potential. A coupling between the two components is introduced through the relation $\rho^{de}=\beta\rho^Q$, where $\beta$ denotes the dark energy coupling parameter. From causality arguments, the admissible range of $\beta$ is constrained as $0<\beta<-\frac{1}{3\omega}$. The structural properties of such compact stars are then analysed by varying $\beta$ within this range. Solution of the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations yields a maximum mass of $2.012~ M_{\odot}$ with a corresponding radius of $\approx 11$ km. Notably, for a fixed $\omega$, both the stellar mass and radius are found to decrease with increasing $\beta$. The model is further examined through causality, energy, and stability conditions, all of which are satisfied, thereby ensuring physical viability. Finally, the framework is applied to estimate radii of several compact star candidates identified as strange quark stars admixed with dark energy, with predictions showing close agreement with recent observational results.
item.dc:creator: Rohit Roy, Koushik Ballav Goswami, Debadri Bhattacharjee, Pradip Kumar Chattopadhyay

item.title: Gravitational redshift of broadband relativistic quantum photons
item.description: arXiv:2504.03956v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gravitational redshift is a key prediction of general relativity that has been experimentally verified. Nevertheless, its existence in the context of relativistic and quantum physics has not yet been established. We employ linearized quantum gravity to study the effects of quantum coherence on gravitational redshift of broadband photons that interact with a planet via graviton exchange. We find that gravitational redshift, as predicted by general relativity, occurs when the initial photonic state contains no quantum coherence between orthogonal photonic modes, such as position states. If quantum coherence is initially present, different photonic modes overlap, a genuine quantum correction occurs solely for single-photon states. Our work not only explains gravitational redshift as the interaction of gravitons and photons in flat spacetime, but also shows that deviations from the theory occur already at low energies when quantum interference of photonic states is important.
item.dc:creator: David Edward Bruschi, Alessio Lapponi, Alessandro Ferreri, Andreas Wolfgang Schell

item.title: Acoustic gravitational waves beyond leading order in bubble over Hubble radius
item.description: arXiv:2504.08037v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We calculate the gravitational wave power spectrum from sound waves in a cosmological first order phase transition in the unexplored regime of large bubbles, by which we mean that the mean bubble spacing $R_*$ is a non-negligible fraction of the Hubble length $\mathcal{H}_*^{-1}$, i.e. $R_*\mathcal{H}_* \lesssim \mathcal{O}(1)$. Since the amplitude of the gravitational wave signal increases with $R_*\mathcal{H}_*$, this is also the loud signal regime. In this regime the effects of gravity, hitherto neglected, become relevant. We carry out the calculation in cosmological perturbation theory expanding in the parameter $R_*\mathcal{H}_*$, or bubble over Hubble radius. The leading order term is the standard result for acoustic production of gravitational waves. At next-to-leading order we find three novel contributions: two contributions arise from general relativistic corrections to the dynamics of both sound and gravitational waves. A third contribution comes from gravitational waves induced by curvature perturbations. These contributions suppress the gravitational wave peak amplitude. The suppression factor, with respect to the leading order contribution, scales as $(R_*\mathcal{H}_*)^2$, and also depends on other transition parameters, such as the sound speed $c_s$, the duration of the acoustic source, and the peak wavenumber of the velocity field $k_p$. In a simplified model of the velocity field, we find that the suppression factor lies between $2\%$ and $15\%$ when $R_*\mathcal{H}_* \simeq 0.5$, but is independent of the root mean squared fluid velocity. We provide analytical approximations to the next-to-leading order corrections, and a recipe to join them smoothly across different frequency regimes. Our work improves the precision of the current estimations of the gravitational wave power spectrum in the relatively unexplored regime of phase transition with large bubbles.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Giombi, Jani Dahl, Mark Hindmarsh

item.title: Reassessing the foundations of Metric-Affine Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2505.05349v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We reassess foundational aspects of Metric-Affine Gravity (MAG) in light of the Dressing Field Method, a tool allowing to systematically build gauge-invariant field variables. To get MAG started, one has to deal with the problem of "gauge translations". We first recall that Cartan geometry is the proper mathematical foundation for gauge theories of gravity, and that this problem never arises in that framework, which still allows to clarify the geometric status of gauge translations. Then, we show how the MAG kinematics is obtained via dressing in a technically streamlined way, which highlights that it reduces to a Cartan-geometric kinematics.
item.dc:creator: J. Fran\c{c}ois, L. Ravera

item.title: Collective Properties of Gravitational Perturbations in Thermal Environments on a Dynamical Background
item.description: arXiv:2510.22346v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A thermal plasma dresses soft gauge fields, turning them into collective modes with a plasmon gap and Landau damping. In this paper, we ask whether a thermal radiation plasma does the same to gravitational perturbations. For gravity, the thermal soft scale coincides with the Hubble rate. Any such gap therefore lies at the horizon scale, where the expansion of the background cannot be neglected. We model radiation by a conformal scalar and compute its linear response to metric perturbations directly on a flat FLRW background. We test this response against the diffeomorphism Ward identities. The adiabatic dispersion relation yields a gapped collective mode with $\omega_p^2 = 8\mathcal{H}^2/5$, where $\mathcal{H}$ is the conformal Hubble rate. The imaginary part of its frequency, however, is dominated by the background expansion and does not represent Landau damping. In the radiation background, the tensor modes obey a real-time integro-differential equation that reproduces Weinberg's damping of gravitational waves. The initial-time boundary of the retarded response keeps superhorizon modes frozen until horizon reentry despite the gap. The superhorizon growth found in earlier analyses arises from discarding the memory of the retarded response and from a local-equilibrium state prescription that violates the Ward identities. More generally, the Ward identities forbid any local state response beyond the collisionless kernel.
item.dc:creator: Atsuhisa Ota

item.title: Black hole binaries in shift-symmetric Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
item.description: arXiv:2511.19073v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In shift-symmetric Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity, stationary black holes have a non-vanishing scalar charge. During the inspiral, the phase evolution is modified by several effects,primarily an additional scalar dipole radiation, which enters at -1PN order. Including corrections up to 2PN, this effect accelerates the inspiral when compared to general relativity, but changes in the conservative dynamics may do the opposite. Using fully non-linear numerical simulations of quasi-circular, comparable mass binaries, we characterize the late stages of the orbital dynamics. We find that the overall effect is still an accelerated merger phase for the modified gravity case, but noticeably less than predicted by PN alone, which we relate to the conservative dynamics, showing that at the late inspiral stage more energy must be emitted in scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity to induce a given change in frequency. In longer signals, this may lead to a distinctive frequency evolution relative to general relativity as the binary approaches merger, but its effect close to merger is to suppress the difference with GR. This work suggests we may need to revisit existing constraints on the theory that are obtained assuming PN approximations apply up to merger, or based on order by order approximations that neglect backreaction effects on the metric, and shows the importance of including non-linear effects that modify the gravitational sector in the strong field regime.
item.dc:creator: Maxence Corman, Llibert Arest\'e Sal\'o, Katy Clough

item.title: Symmetries of cosmological perturbations: The residual low-multipole ambiguity
item.description: arXiv:2601.04144v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In cosmology, long-wavelength modes are related to large-gauge transformations (LGT), i.e. changes of coordinates that modify the physical geometry of the cosmological patch. These LGTs stand as bona-fide symmetries of cosmological perturbation theory with various applications, from consistency relations constraining cosmological correlators to non-linear conservation laws in the separate-universe approach. In this work, we revisit LGTs and derive two new results. First, we show that the global symmetries already identified in the literature can be extended to local infinite-dimensional symmetries. The associated generators depend on arbitrary functions of time, and generate low-multipole modes that modify the mean curvature energy and the angular momentum of the patch, demonstrating their physical nature. We propose to interpret these low-multipole soft modes as a new cosmological-frame ambiguity that needs to be fixed prior to evaluating cosmological observables. Second, we demonstrate that the adiabatic cosmological perturbations generated by LGTs deform but preserve all the explicit and hidden Killing symmetries of the background geometry. As such, long-wavelength modes stand as a concrete example of algebraically-special cosmological perturbations of Petrov-type O, and inherit the conformal group as isometries and a set of four deformed Killing-Yano tensors and their associated Killing tensors. This opens the possibility to study their effect on cosmological observables in a fully analytic manner.
item.dc:creator: Jibril Ben Achour, Etera Livine, Vincent Vennin

item.title: Looking for non-gaussianity in Pulsar Timing Arrays through the four point correlator
item.description: arXiv:2603.12311v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pulsar Timing Arrays have recently reported strong evidence for a stochastic gravitational wave background. In standard analyses, it is modeled through pulsar-dependent Fourier coefficients assumed to follow gaussian statistics, so that the signal is fully characterized by its two-point function. However, if the background arises from a finite population of inspiralling supermassive black hole binaries, non-gaussian features may emerge, making the determination of higher-order correlators essential. In this work, we compute the complete four-point correlator of the stochastic gravitational wave background Fourier coefficients for four arbitrary pulsar positions, identifying it as the leading probe of non-gaussianity. The result separates into a gaussian contribution, proportional to the square of the two-point function, and a genuinely non-gaussian connected component, whose non-trivial angular dependence generalizes the Hellings and Downs correlation to four pulsars. This angular structure depends only on averages of products of antenna pattern functions, and is therefore expected to be independent of the specific physical origin of the background. We further propose to incorporate the four-point correlator into the parameter-estimation pipeline by deriving a marginalized likelihood that perturbatively accounts for non-gaussian effects. Our results provide the theoretical framework to search for non-gaussian features in pulsar timing array data, opening the way to a more complete characterization of gravitational-wave backgrounds.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Kuntz, Clemente Smarra, Massimo Vaglio

item.title: Matching Tidal Deformability (Wilson) Coefficients to Black Hole Love Numbers in Higher-Curvature Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2604.04259v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a consistent mapping between tidal deformability coefficients (tidal Love numbers) and Wilson coefficients in effective field theory (EFT) descriptions of higher-curvature theories of gravity. In this work, we focus on the connection between the static response of a non-spinning black hole and the corresponding Wilson coefficient governing tidal imprints in gravitational-wave signals. We analyze a set of control cases to identify the key ingredients required for a systematic computation and matching procedure. In doing so, we highlight shortcomings in existing results that rely on the standard matching approach used in General Relativity when applied to higher-curvature gravity theories. As an explicit demonstration, we compute the relevant coefficients for cubic gravity theories. Our findings bridge an important gap in the correspondence between tidal Love numbers and Wilson coefficients in EFT extensions of General Relativity, which had not been thoroughly explored previously.
item.dc:creator: Luohan Wang, Luis Lehner, Mait\'a Micol, Riccardo Sturani

item.title: Novel Ringdown Tests of General Relativity with Black Hole Graybody Factors
item.description: arXiv:2604.11895v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present GreyRing, a new model for the post-merger signal in black-hole binary coalescences based on the graybody factor of the remnant. The model accurately reproduces the full frequency-domain ringdown signal of a large set of comparable-mass, aligned-spin numerical relativity waveforms, achieving mismatches of order ${\cal O}(10^{-6})$ for the dominant $(\ell,m)=(2,2)$ mode, and typically outperforming state-of-the-art time-domain models. Building on this model, we introduce a novel consistency test of strong gravity based on the graybody factor: the remnant mass and spin inferred from GreyRing can be compared with those obtained through standard black hole spectroscopy. This agnostic test relies exclusively on the post-merger signal and does not require the inclusion of overtones or the choice of very early ringdown starting times, combining the advantages of inspiral-merger-ringdown consistency tests and traditional black hole spectroscopy. We apply the test to GW250114 and find that the remnant mass and spin inferred from GreyRing are consistent with those measured from the full signal. Remarkably, the inferred parameters can be measured with a precision comparable to, or slightly better than, that achieved with standard black-hole spectroscopy. Our graybody-factor waveform model allows for new precision tests of strong gravity using the ringdown signal.
item.dc:creator: Romeo Felice Rosato, Francesco Crescimbeni, Sophia Yi, Emanuele Berti, Paolo Pani

item.title: Bilinear products and the orthogonality of quasinormal modes on hyperboloidal foliations
item.description: arXiv:2604.13182v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We explore the properties of bilinear products for black-hole quasinormal modes (QNMs) formulated on hyperboloidal foliations. We find that, although QNM solutions are smooth and finite on future-directed hyperboloids, the integrand of the bilinear form with respect to which the modes are orthogonal is still divergent. This is a result of the reflection (equivalently, CPT) transformation required in the definition of the products, which modifies the behaviour of the integrand at the boundaries. We present several regularisation procedures that yield a finite and well-defined bilinear form. In addition, we examine an alternative definition of the bilinear products that incorporates flux contributions, discussing its advantages and limitations. Finally, we define the QNM excitation factors and coefficients within the hyperboloidal framework in terms of the bilinear products, and compute them explicitly for a choice of mode numbers and constant initial data. For concreteness, we work with the QNMs associated to scalar perturbations of the Schwarzschild family of spacetimes.
item.dc:creator: Marica Minucci, Rodrigo Panosso Macedo, Christiana Pantelidou, Laura Sberna

item.title: Analytical primordial power spectra from a potential dominated pre-inflationary bounce in a closed universe
item.description: arXiv:2605.04755v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The CMB TT spectrum is suppressed at large scales, a feature that may originate from pre-inflationary dynamics in a closed universe. We study the primordial power spectrum for a potential dominated pre-inflationary bounce in a spatially closed universe by extending the analytical approximations of Thavanesan et al.~\cite{Thavanesan2021}, and find that it exhibits the same suppression trend as the KICI and emergent scenarios. Using the analytical approximation, we further show that the resulting CMB TT spectra for the pre-inflationary bounce scenario are the same as those of the KICI and emergent scenarios, indicating that the pre-inflationary bounce scenario can account for the large scale suppression of the CMB TT spectrum as well as the KICI and emergent scenarios. This extends the potential independent analytical approach to a potential dominated pre-inflationary bounce, providing a new scenario that accounts for the observed large scale suppression of the CMB TT spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Qihong Huang

item.title: Near-Horizon Deformation of Metric and the Black Hole Instability
item.description: arXiv:2606.02066v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent time-domain analyses suggest that black hole stability may be sensitive to localized near-horizon geometric deformations, while the underlying spectral mechanism remain unclear. In this work, after verifying the instability of the model in the time domain, we systematically investigate quasi-normal mode spectra under static localized non-positive perturbations within a frequency-domain framework. We find that such deformations generically induce a new purely imaginary mode. As the deformation approaches the horizon, the imaginary part of this mode increases and eventually enters the upper half complex-frequency plane, signaling the onset of black hole instability. Numerical results reveal clear scaling relations between the critical distance for instability and the deformation strength. We further derive rigorous proofs for our discoveries in frequency domain. These results demonstrate that black hole stability under long scale is conditionally sensitive to localized deformation of metric near the horizon and establish a unified spectral framework for understanding their induced instabilities.
item.dc:creator: Shi-Jie Ma, Zhan-Feng Mai, Run-Qiu Yang

item.title: Binary Black Hole Coalescence and the Dynamics of Scalar Hair in Einstein-Maxwell-Scalar Theory
item.description: arXiv:2606.21549v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the head-on coalescence of charged binary black holes in Einstein-Maxwell-Scalar (EMS) theory using numerical relativity. The binaries are built from charged puncture initial data representing two Reissner-Nordstr\"om black holes immersed in a purely kinetic scalar perturbation: the scalar field initially vanishes, while its conjugate momentum provides a small seed for the instability. We evolve the coupled gravitational, electromagnetic, and scalar sectors and monitor the apparent horizons, the emitted radiation, and the scalar field on the horizons. Our simulations show that the nonminimal electromagnetic-scalar coupling can dynamically trigger the growth of scalar hair even when the individual black holes are initially scalar-free. The subsequent evolution depends on the coupling parameter $\alpha_0$ and on the charge-to-mass ratio of the remnant. For weak coupling, or when charge cancellation suppresses the electromagnetic source after the merger, the scalar field is radiated away or absorbed by the final horizon, and the system dynamically descalarizes. For sufficiently strong coupling and nonzero remnant charge, the scalar field remains finite, and the final black hole approaches a scalarized configuration. For binaries with equal charge-to-mass ratios, $q_1=q_2=0.1$, our simulations identify a transition region between $1900<\alpha_0<2000$, that separates descalarized and scalarized remnants. The coalescence also excites scalar radiation whose time profile is qualitatively correlated with the dominant gravitational-wave mode during the nonlinear stage of the collision. These results provide a binary realization of scalarization/descalarization transitions in EMS theory and show that the fate of scalar hair is controlled by the interplay between the scalar coupling and the charge content of the remnant.
item.dc:creator: Jean Pierre D\'iaz, P. A. Gonz\'alez, Eleftherios Papantonopoulos, Yerko V\'asquez

item.title: Non-Metricity Corrections Approach to Alleviate $H_0$ Tension: The Logarithmic and Nonlinear $f(Q)$ Models
item.description: arXiv:2606.22262v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The persistent discrepancy between early-time and late-Universe measurements of the Hubble constant commonly known as the $H_0$ tension remains one of the most pressing open questions in modern cosmology. In this work, we explore whether modifications to the gravitational sector, specifically within the framework of symmetric teleparallel gravity, can offer a viable pathway toward alleviating this tension. We consider two functional forms of $f(Q)$ gravity: a logarithmic model and a nonlinear saturation model, both of which introduce geometric corrections to the standard expansion history without invoking a cosmological constant. Constraining these models through a Bayesian MCMC analysis against a comprehensive suite of observational data, including cosmic chronometers, Type Ia supernova compilations (Pantheon, Pantheon$+$SH0ES, and DES SN5YR), and BAO measurements from SDSS and DESI, we find that both models remain statistically competitive with $\Lambda$CDM. The logarithmic model, in particular, consistently infers intermediate values of $H_0$ between the \textit{Planck} and SH0ES benchmarks across all dataset combinations, and carries lower AIC and BIC penalties, establishing it as the more promising candidate for partially easing the $H_0$ tension within a modified gravity framework.
item.dc:creator: Rahul Bhagat, Kesava Chodavarapu, B. Mishra

item.title: Quintic Modification to Lifshitz Quasi-topological Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2606.24835v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend the analysis of Lifshitz black holes to quintic order in five-dimensional quasi-topological gravity coupled to a massive Abelian vector field. Starting from a static ansatz with a constant-curvature horizon, we derive the reduced field equations and identify the radially conserved quantity of the one-dimensional effective system. We then analyze the algebraic conditions that permit Lifshitz backgrounds, both in the absence and in the presence of the massive vector field. Since closed-form black-hole solutions are not available for the generic quintic theory, we construct numerical solutions by integrating the field equations outward from regular near-horizon data. We present solutions for the relativistic branch \(z=1\) and the Lifshitz branch \(z=2\), covering the three horizon topologies \(k=-1,0,+1\). The numerical profiles remain qualitatively consistent with those found previously in cubic and quartic quasi-topological Lifshitz gravity. A controlled planar comparison through the genuine quartic point \(\hat\mu_5=0\) further shows that the very small quintic couplings used in the representative examples produce nearly quartic profiles, whereas larger admissible values of \(\hat\mu_5\) lead to clearly resolved changes in both the normalized radial profiles and the Hawking temperature. We also compute the Wald entropy and Hawking temperature and examine the thermal behavior through dimensionless logarithmic temperature--entropy plots. For the representative branches considered here, the heat capacity is positive. For a fixed-theory planar \(z=2\) family, the conserved radial charge is further used to determine the energy density; the differential and integrated first laws are verified numerically to the precision of the computation, and the corresponding Helmholtz free-energy density is found to be negative relative to the Lifshitz vacuum normalization adopted here.
item.dc:creator: A. Bazrafshan, A. R. Olamaei, M. Ghanaatian

item.title: Tidal Forces in the Presence of Torsion and Nonmetricity
item.description: arXiv:2606.27433v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work investigates how torsion and nonmetricity modify tidal accelerations in metric-affine gravity. We derive a projected deviation equation that generalizes the standard geodesic deviation equation to metric-affine geometry, and apply it to the relative acceleration of neighboring autoparallels in the weak-field, nonrelativistic limit. In this regime, the tidal acceleration separates into the usual Newtonian contribution and linear post-Riemannian corrections sourced by torsion and non-metricity. By decomposing torsion and nonmetricity into their irreducible Lorentz components, we identify the corresponding signatures in the tidal tensor and discuss to what extent these contributions can be distinguished. We then show how future direct tidal measurements could be translated into benchmark bounds on post-Riemannian tidal contributions, assuming probe dynamics sensitive to the affine connection. Our results suggest that the tidal acceleration may provide a systematic route toward probing post-Riemannian spacetime features in the future.
item.dc:creator: Armin van de Venn, Marcelo Netz-Marzola, David Vasak, J\"urgen Struckmeier

item.title: Gravitational lensing by extremal rotating black holes in the strong deflection limit
item.description: arXiv:2606.29418v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the strong deflection regime, light rays passing close to an astrophysical black hole may remain trapped near unstable photon orbits for a long time before escaping to infinity. The traditional strong-deflection limit, which accurately describes the logarithmic divergence of the deflection angle for spherically symmetric and slowly rotating black holes, breaks down when the relevant prograde critical photon orbit coincides with the degenerate horizon of an extremal rotating black hole. We present a new strong deflection limit expansion for this horizon critical orbit, covering a general class of extremal rotating black holes. We show that the deflection angle exhibits a stronger power-law divergence in addition to the logarithmic divergence. For an adequate description of higher-order images, additional terms in the expansion must be retained. We first study prograde gravitational lensing in the equatorial plane and then extend the analysis to quasi-equatorial motion, which allows us to calculate the magnification of the higher-order images and the position of the caustic points. We finally apply the general framework to explicit examples, including the Kerr, Kerr-Newman, and Kerr-Sen metrics.
item.dc:creator: Fabiano Feleppa, Valerio Bozza, Welmoed Marit de Graaf

item.title: Exploring Exact Einsteinian Black Hole Physics in Dark Matter Environment: Ray Tracing, Stability, Eikonal QNMs and Thermodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2607.08792v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the recent rebuttal of black hole--dark matter solutions based on velocity-matching, we reconstruct the spacetime by treating the dark matter halo density directly as an energy-density source in the Einstein field equations. We obtain an exact static, spherically symmetric black hole solution and investigate the effects of the halo on its geometry, optical properties, quasinormal modes, and thermodynamics. Using null geodesics, we show that the halo modifies photon trajectories, shifts the circular photon orbit, and enlarges the photon sphere and apparent shadow. The Lyapunov exponent of the unstable null orbit further determines the eikonal quasinormal modes, yielding explicit halo-induced corrections to their oscillation and damping rates. We also compute the mass, Hawking temperature, entropy, heat capacity, and Gibbs free energy to characterize the thermodynamic stability and phase structure. We find that the dark matter halo enlarges the domain of thermodynamic stability and introduces nontrivial phase behavior absent in the Schwarzschild case, demonstrating that astrophysical dark matter environments can leave potentially observable imprints on black hole observables.
item.dc:creator: David Senjaya

item.title: Scalar-induced gravitational waves from a box-shaped curvature power spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2607.10730v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the stochastic background of gravitational waves (GWs) produced at second order in cosmological perturbation theory by a primordial curvature power spectrum that is flat in $\ln k$ over a finite band $[k_-,k_+]=[k_*e^{-\Delta},k_*e^{+\Delta}]$ and vanishes elsewhere. This logarithmic box interpolates between a monochromatic spectrum as $\Delta\to0$ and a locally scale-invariant plateau as $\Delta\to\infty$, and its sharp boundaries make the geometry of the source convolution unusually transparent. Working in the radiation era, we reduce the convolution to a compact integral over the overlap between the momentum triangle and the box, and evaluate it analytically in two regimes. For a narrow box we show that, to leading order in the width, the spectrum equals the Dirac-spectrum result multiplied by a purely geometric overlap factor $\Phi_{\rm box}(\kappa,\Delta)$; this factor turns the infrared slope from $k^{3}\ln^{2}k$ into $k^{2}\ln^{2}k$ at a break $k_b=2k_*\sinh\Delta$. For a broad box we separate the lower edge, the scale-invariant interior, and the upper edge, derive the leading behaviour in each (an infrared $k^{3}\ln^{2}k$ rise, a scale-invariant plateau, and a quartic cut-off at the hard endpoint $k=2k_+$), and combine them into a single uniform formula cast as a product of two universal, $\Delta$-independent edge functions. We also provide an integral-free closed-form surrogate for these edge functions for use in parameter scans.
item.dc:creator: Zu-Cheng Chen, Lang Liu

item.title: Kerr black holes without primary hairs
item.description: arXiv:2607.14910v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a class of regular axisymmetric black hole geometries fully characterized by the parameters $\{{\cal M},a\}$ and possessing the Kerr event horizon. This family interpolates between regular spacetimes, configurations with integrable singularities, and the Kerr solution as a limiting case. Its main features are: (i) the existence of quasi-extremal configurations without requiring $a \approx {\cal M}$; and (ii) a possible framework toward an analytical description of Kerr black hole formation from an initially regular configuration.
item.dc:creator: J Ovalle

item.title: Phantom-Divide Crossing in Barrow-Tsallis Holographic Dark Energy with a Scale-Dependent Barrow Exponent
item.description: arXiv:2607.26089v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Phantom-divide crossing is studied in spatially flat cosmologies with standard Friedmann equations, separately conserved holographic dark energy and a barotropic fluid, and the future event horizon as the infrared cutoff. The horizon entropy and dark-energy density are prescribed by $ S_h=S_{\mathrm{BH}}F(L) $ and $ \rho_X\propto F(L)/L^2 $, where $ F(L) $ is smooth, positive and single-valued, with $ \chi=\mathrm{d}\ln F/\mathrm{d}\ln L $. For $ w_b>-1 $, $ 0<\Omega_X<1 $ and $ \chi<2 $ along the trajectory, at most one phantom-divide crossing is possible. If a crossing occurs, dark energy passes from the quintessence regime into the phantom regime at a maximum of the horizon radius. The crossing kinematics determines the local entropy-scaling dimension and the sign of the local Chevallier-Polarski-Linder coefficient. Integrating the locally prescribed scale-dependent Barrow exponent reconstructs the Barrow-Tsallis entropy function. A necessary and sufficient event-horizon consistency criterion selects admissible solutions, whose late-time asymptotics include de Sitter states, Type III and Big Rip singularities, and accelerated power-law expansion under the corresponding parameter conditions. A numerical comparison with a constant Barrow exponent distinguishes the occurrence of a crossing from the effect of exponent variation on late-time evolution. With an adiabatic barotropic fluid, additive total entropy and an equilibrium Gibbs relation for dark energy, the generalized second law fails at the kinematic crossing for positive barotropic-fluid entropy and finite nonzero dark-energy temperature. The divergence of $ c_a^2 $ shows that the purely barotropic adiabatic description of perturbations breaks down. This divergence alone does not establish physical instability.
item.dc:creator: D. A. Yerokhin

item.title: Disformal Maps: Classification and Singular Dynamics
item.description:
arXiv:2608.04094v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Being agnostic about the field content of a gravitational system, we consider a general disformal transformation of the metric, $g_{\mu
u}=C h_{\mu
u}+D t_{\mu
u}$, on a four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold. Using the Cayley-Hamilton theorem, we derive an explicit formula for the inverse disformed metric. Implementing the Hawking-Ellis classification, we categorize disformal transformations into four types: Type I, II, III, and IV, based on possible Jordan block structures. We further identify the Segre subclasses from the eigenvalues. We derive explicit relations between the Cayley-Hamilton degree of $t_{\mu
u}$, its Hawking-Ellis type, and its Segre subclass, restricting the possible types from the degree alone. In some cases, the type can be determined without even performing a full Jordan decomposition. For singular transformations, when new dynamical degrees of freedom emerge, we obtain the form of their corresponding mimetic energy-momentum tensor $T^\star_{\mu
u}$. Within the polynomial sector, the Hawking-Ellis types of $t_{\mu
u}$ and $T^\star_{\mu
u}$ always coincide for Type I. For Types II and III it can differ, while Type IV is preserved generically but can reduce to Type I when the complex pair is mapped to a repeated real eigenvalue. This makes it possible to infer physical properties of $T^\star_{\mu
u}$ directly from the Hawking-Ellis type of $t_{\mu
u}$. We apply our setup to scalar and gauge fields. We find a new pure-disformal scalar-gauge family yielding irrotational perfect fluids, including barotropic fluids with an arbitrary constant equation-of-state parameter. Two scalar fields realize all four types and the reductions from Types II and IV to Type I. This framework applies to the kinematical and dynamical study of invertible and non-invertible disformal transformations with different field content.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Ali Gorji, Pavel Jirou\v{s}ek, Alexander Vikman, Masahide Yamaguchi

item.title: Innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) of arbitrary-mass compact binaries with spins at the fourth post-Newtonian order
item.description: arXiv:2608.07756v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute, up to 4th post-Newtonian (4PN) order, the gauge-invariant stability criterion determining the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) for arbitrary-mass compact binaries with spins aligned with the orbital angular momentum. Our calculation, a perturbation analysis, incorporates spin-orbit and spin-spin contributions, both up to next-to-next-to-leading order, as well as leading-order cubic and quartic spin contributions, all calculated in prior works within the effective-field-theory (EFT) Hamiltonian formalism. In the test-mass limit, we recover the Kerr ISCO truncated at 4PN order. Estimating the ISCO shift at first order in the mass ratio and comparing our results with numerical gravitational self-force (GSF) calculations, we find good agreement for retrograde spin (the smallest discrepancy being obtained for maximal retrograde spin) and moderate prograde spin. For nearly maximal prograde spin, the PN approach fails to determine the ISCO, for it is close to the black hole (BH) horizon. We also estimate the ISCO shift due to the test-particle spin and compare our result with the exact prediction from the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon (MPD) equations for a spinning particle orbiting a Kerr black hole. Finally, we discuss the stability and the ISCO of corotating black-hole binaries.
item.dc:creator: Luc Blanchet, David Langlois, Etienne Ligout

item.title: Cosmological Vacuum Decays from Schwinger-Keldysh Formalism
item.description: arXiv:2608.12736v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we take a first step to a stochastic real-time description of the vacuum phase transitions in a radiation-dominated FLRW universe from the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism. By splitting the phase transition field $\Phi$ into the long-wavelength mode $\phi$ and the short-wavelength mode $\sigma$ and tracing over the latter as the environment, we obtain a classical Langevin-type equation-of-motion for the long-wavelength field $\phi$, where the quantum effects are encoded in a non-Markov memory kernel and a non-Gaussian noise. As a phenomenological example, we start from a polynomial potential and a thermalized initial state, and study the structure of the memory kernel as well as the correlation functions of the noise term. Further extensions remain possible to describe the whole dynamics of cosmological first-order phase transitions via numerical simulations.
item.dc:creator: Zi-Yan Yuwen

item.title: Static Magnetic Brane Solutions in Quartic Quasi-Topological Gravity with Power-Law Maxwell Nonlinear Electrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2608.15178v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate static magnetic brane solutions in (n+1)-dimensional quartic quasi-topological gravity coupled to power-law Maxwell nonlinear electrodynamics. We derive the corresponding solutions and analyze their geometric and physical properties. We observe that the solutions are horizonless and free of curvature singularities in the physically accessible region, while the spacetime generally exhibits a conical singularity with a nonzero angular deficit at the lower radial endpoint. We demonstrate that the endpoint is independent of the higher-curvature couplings lambda, mu, and c, whereas the near-endpoint geometry is mainly controlled by the magnetic parameter q and the nonlinear parameter s. At large radial distances, we find that the higher-curvature couplings govern the asymptotic behavior of the metric. We also establish that finite asymptotic solutions require 1/2 < s <= 2 and analyze the dependence of the angular deficit on q, s, and the endpoint parameter rho_+. Using the counterterm method, we calculate the conserved mass density and show that the static magnetic brane carries no net electric charge. Finally, we verify that the power-law Maxwell theory recovers linear Maxwell electrodynamics at s=1 and Einstein gravity when lambda=mu=c=0.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Alizadeh, Saheb Soroushfar, Mohammad Ghanaatian, Sayyed Mehrab Ramezani, Sudhaker Upadhyay, Kairat Myrzakulov

item.title: Gravitational lensing outside and inside of a marginally unstable photon sphere at a $Z_2$-symmetric wormhole throat in strong deflection limits
item.description: arXiv:2608.23269v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The deflection angles of rays diverge logarithmically near outside and inside of a photon sphere in usual strong deflection limits and the rays near the photon sphere could be detected by near-future space observations on black hole shadows. On the other hand, we show that the deflection angles of the rays near the photon sphere at a throat of a $Z_2$-symmetric wormhole, as an example among some commonly used types of wormholes or simple wormholes, which is often studied by the Event Horizon Telescope collaborations, diverge in power law but not logarithmically. This is because the $Z_2$-symmetric wormhole has a marginally unstable photon sphere at the throat and it has neither a common nor simple but special property. We investigate gravitational lensing of the rays nearly outside and inside of the marginally unstable photon sphere at the throat in a class of $Z_2$-symmetric wormholes in the strong deflection limits. We use a numerical method to calculate the deflection angles diverging in power law and we apply it to the commonly-used simple wormhole spacetime, a Damour-Solodukhin wormhole spacetime, and a Simpson-Visser black-bounce spacetime. Our numerical results imply universal property of the deflection angle of the rays near the marginally unstable photon sphere on $Z_2$-symmetric wormhole throat in the strong deflection limits as similar to the deflection angles of ray bent by a marginally unstable photon sphere off a throat in the strong deflection limits which have a different power. We also correct the coefficients of power-law divergent terms of the deflection angles of the rays bent nearly outside of the marginally unstable photon sphere at the $Z_2$-symmetric wormhole throat in a semi-analytic approach investigated by the author and others.
item.dc:creator: Naoki Tsukamoto

item.title: Gravitational Radiation from Shockwave Scattering in the Self-Force EFT
item.description: arXiv:2609.09378v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the high-energy collision of two spinless bodies within the Self-Force Effective Field Theory (EFT), taking one of them to be massless and highly energetic, such that it generates a gravitational shockwave (GSW) background. The GSW is perturbed by the second body, either massless or massive, satisfying respectively $E_2/E_1\ll1$ or $m_2/E_1\ll1$. Although the Self-Force expansion for shockwaves is frame-dependent, we freely choose a frame in which this EFT manifests its power, obtaining results valid to all orders in Newton's constant that make the underlying resummation patterns evident. Specifically, we push the expansion to 1SF order and prove the all-order vanishing of the so-called recoil operators in light-cone gauge. We obtain the exact graviton propagator on the shockwave background, matching previous results, and use it to compute the on-shell waveform at 1SF order in momentum space, specialising to the massless-massless collision. The waveform is computed to all orders in the Post-Minkowskian, or weak-field, expansion. In the trans-Planckian regime, its resummed form is proved to yield a UV-finite angular spectrum of radiated energy.
item.dc:creator: Emanuele Rosi

item.title: Periodic Orbits of Van der Waals Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2609.15278v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Black holes in asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime whose extended-phase-space thermodynamics reproduces that of a van der Waals fluid exactly form a distinctive class, the van der Waals black holes (VBHs). The timelike geodesics of VBHs are solved, their periodic orbits are catalogued, and the gravitational waves emitted along them are computed, so as to trace how the thermodynamic pressure P and the molecular-volume parameter b shape the orbital dynamics. Integrating the geodesic equations numerically yields the energy, angular momentum and radius of the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) and maps out the family of bound orbits. To delimit the parameter window in which the effective potential stays well behaved, we introduce a critical angular momentum Ls. Within the orbit-classification scheme, we compute the energies corresponding to rational q for several parameter sets and display the resulting orbits. The waveforms produced along these orbits are generated within the "Kludge" formalism, which makes it possible to quantify the imprint of b on the wave amplitude and on the period. Both the orbital architecture and the gravitational-wave signature turn out to be strongly sensitive to b.
